rows.reason: Execution on 'That he stayed about ten minutes with their father' says 'Line 5 does say he sat about ten minutes... inside the window'; 'sat about ten minutes' is line 4, outside the 5-8 window.

Execution on 'A dance with the eldest Miss Bennet' asserts the assembly is 'weeks after this visit'; the passage gives no such interval (and his dancing with the eldest is at line 60, not lines 36-41).
hintCore 'Find the words obliged to be in town' quotes the answer clause itself; the key is a paraphrase of those words, so the hint coaches (R572).
Lines 13-16 'she began to fear... flying about... never settled' support the key alone; distractors checked against lines 10, 16-18; hint locates without giving; walk accurate.
'party entered the assembly-room' (line 21) and 'a large party' (line 17) fix the group sense; ball/celebration/political/everybody distractors ruled out; walk accurate.
Lines 21-23 give five altogether; minus Bingley leaves two sisters, the eldest's husband and another young man; earlier reports correctly treated as superseded.
Twelve/seven and six are reports ('a report', 'hearing that'), five is what entered; key is the only reading the lines support; executions true; hint and walk accurate.
'pleasant countenance' (24) and 'forbidding, disagreeable countenance' (34) both fit face/look only; manners/permission/good-name/count distractors ruled out.
Lines 27-29 give person, features and the ten-thousand-a-year report; Derbyshire estate (33) comes after the turn; tallest/dancing/kindness unsupported.

Option 'They decided he was less good-looking than Mr Bingley' is TRUE of lines 34-35 as an outcome ('forbidding, disagreeable countenance... unworthy to be compared with his friend'); execution says only that it 'reverses line 30' and the tag (agent-patient-reversal) does not name the actual mistake, which is taking the result for the cause.
Sentence at line 39 sits between Bingley's dancing (37) and Darcy's not dancing (39-41); key only defensible reading; distractors and executions true.

Lines 39-40 'once with Mrs. Hurst and once with Miss Bingley' give the key alone; distractors checked. Note: appended 'In the window, line 39 answers the stem' clause on the first option is truncated noise, not false.

hintCore 'Whose opinion is this - the writer's own, or the room's?' offers a binary whose second half is the key ('the room's quick opinion'), so it coaches (R572). Also: option 'said nothing to anybody all evening' is tagged en-wrong-scope-retrieval but its execution refutes it from line 41 inside the window, so the tag does not name the mistake.
hintCore 'The words one of her daughters are the clue' quotes the key's own phrase ('rude about one of her daughters'), so it coaches (R572).
hintCore 'What does scarcity of gentlemen mean?' asks the child to define the exact phrase whose definition is the key ('not enough gentlemen'), so it coaches (R572).
walkScript ends 'The room hears nothing of this'; the passage never says so (line 48 says only that Darcy stood near enough for Elizabeth to overhear).
Speech opens 'I must have you dance' and closes 'You had much better dance'; key alone defensible; distractors and executions true.
Line 54-56 list who Darcy might stand up with; 'engaged' = dances already promised; marriage/busy/talking/unwilling ruled out; walk accurate.
Lines 57-59 contrast Bingley pleased by many girls with Darcy pleased by none; 'very hard to please' alone fits; fast/shy/tidy/rude ruled out.

walkScript ends 'Putting up with things is the other sense', but the row's own repaired execution states that meaning belongs to TOLERANT and is not a sense of 'tolerable' at all; the walk is wrong about English.
Lines 71-72 'with great spirit... a lively, playful disposition' fix the sense; ghost/anger/quiet/bravery ruled out; walk accurate.
Line 70 'no very cordial feelings' with lines 71-73 'great spirit... delighted in anything ridiculous' give the key; forgiveness/sympathy/unbothered/handsome ruled out.

Key 'never whether the writer agrees' is not the only defensible answer: the narrator characterises directly at lines 24-25 ('good-looking and gentlemanlike... easy, unaffected manners') and lines 72-73 ('a lively, playful disposition'), which supports distractor 'We are told what the writer thinks'. Also hintCore calls Jane Austen 'he'.
Execution on 'The green squares of the fields' says they are 'what they pass over'; line 3 has the HILL rising over the fields, not the travellers passing over them (the walkScript has it right).

hintCore 'Two of these sit in one window only' is false: only the 'eyes fixed... eager' option sits in one window; the lamps option is in neither and the other two use both. Also the lamps option's execution carries an appended clause 'line 9 answers the stem' which is untrue for a what-has-changed question.
hintCore 'Ask what does not belong in a sweet, simple spot' restates the key ('Armed men do not belong in a sweet and simple spot') almost word for word, so it coaches (R572).
Lines 18-19 'behind the peaceful and sunlit countryside there rose ever... the long, gloomy curve of the moor'; houses/countryside/village distractors ruled out; hint non-coaching; walk accurate.

Execution on 'Was covered over by a skirt' opens 'The commonest everyday sense of the word', which is false of 'skirted' and contradicts its own retag note (en-vocab-built-from-parts); the execution no longer describes the tagged mistake.
Lines 32-34 put a mounted soldier on the summit watching the road; 'LIKE an equestrian statue' rules out the statue; heath-clad land is the rise itself; walk accurate.

Stem asks 'What has the moor got in it besides stone?' but the key answers a different question ('The bare moor and the hidden man together chill him'), as do the executions ('rather than what chills him', window 'lines 40 to 46' against a stem window of 40 to 44).

Key 'The gold and the green give way to bare stone' misstates lines 47-51: green is not given for the country behind, the slopes ahead are 'russet and olive' (olive is a green), and they are 'sprinkled with giant boulders', not bare stone. The hint ('The question asks about ahead') also pulls against a key that describes behind-to-ahead.
Lines 59-60 'surmounted by the boars' heads of the Baskervilles'; tracery is the gates, lichens describe the pillars, lamps unstated; walk accurate.
Execution on 'Night had fallen before they reached it' cites 'line 57 has them arriving in a fading light'; 'fading light' is line 73 and line 57 says nothing of light.
Line 74 'draped in ivy' and line 75 'the dark veil' fix the ivy; face-cloth/clipped patches/coat of arms ruled out; walk accurate.

walkScript says 'At line 4 the hill is melancholy before anyone has said a word', but Dr Mortimer speaks at lines 1-2 before it; it also says Nature 'throws at them' where line 28 has 'throw before the carriage'.
Line 3-5 the waiting chair and Farhan's reward; line 47 'you stand up when somebody is about to thank you'; key alone answers why; distractors and executions true.
Lines 7-8 wings pumping 'which is the sign'; key alone fits; board/maths/card ruled out; walk accurate.
Lines 8-9 'they get sad and start bashing themselves against the sides'; football/hand/chrysalis ruled out; walk accurate.
walkScript 'Line 13 says she said it on Monday' is wrong: 'She said it on Monday' is on line 12; line 13 is that they were still asleep on Monday.
Line 17 'The net will not carry flat, so I put four of them in my lunchbox'; sleeve/hidden/warm ruled out; hint non-coaching; walk accurate.
Lines 23-24 'so he knows what they are, which proves they were ready'; key alone; distractors and executions true.
walkScript 'Line 27 says that is what half past two is like' misreports lines 26-27, which say screaming is 'just what Reception is like at half past two'.
Lines 29-30 Mr Okafor says nobody is going up there for a butterfly, not today; beam position is Dilan's report; window and ladder ruled out.
Lines 31-32 'through the serving hatch into the kitchen' fix the opening sense (cf. line 5 'by the hatch'); egg/floor-door/extinguisher ruled out.
Line 32 'would rather not say what I think' with lines 33-34 window 'open all afternoon' give the key; kitchen one is a different butterfly; lunchbox catch unstated.
Lines 38-40 'that will be about the fountain, and the fountain was ages ago and everybody has moved on'; key alone; distractors and executions true.

'It goes well' (21), 'it is a pass' (28), 'Reception are fine' (26) against lines 28-34 losses and Mum called in; key alone; 'knows he went too far' contradicted by his closing expectation of thanks (47).
